title: The papers want {name} dropped
text: Gary Haddon has {name} on the back page after a poor few weeks and says he should make way. {first} has averaged a Player rating of {form} over his last three games. Players who started as a {role_word} this year average a Player rating of {role_avg}.

unanswered.why: You said nothing when the papers went after him
unanswered.text: You say nothing. {first} reads the back page on his own.

choices.label: Rest him this week

effects.why: You dropped him after the papers pushed

choices.result: {name} sits out this week.

choices.label: Keep him in

effects.why: You kept him in when the papers wanted him out

choices.result: {name} stays in the side.

title: Kev Pollard has sprayed you on radio
text: Outer Wing Radio: "{club} have lost their way and the coach has lost the rooms." Do you bite?

choices.label: Hit back in the presser
choices.result: You hit back. The players love it; the board winces.

choices.label: Let your footy do the talking
choices.result: You say nothing. The rooms hear it all week anyway.

title: {name} has been offered a newspaper column
text: A weekly piece in the Sunday paper. Good money, and a lot of opinions.

choices.label: Let him write it

effects.why: You let him write his column

choices.result: {name}'s first column runs on Sunday.

choices.label: Knock it back

effects.why: You knocked back his newspaper column

choices.result: {name} turns the paper down.

title: Footy Tonight want a feature on {name}
text: Trish Lomax wants a week with him. Good for the club, and a lot of spotlight on a kid.

choices.label: Do the feature
choices.result: The feature goes to air. The boys give him a hard time.

choices.label: Keep him out of it
choices.result: No feature. {first} would have liked it.

title: The Siren has your side before it's announced
text: Someone at the club is talking to Gary Haddon.

choices.label: Find the leak
choices.result: You go looking. Everyone feels watched.

choices.label: Let it go
choices.result: You let it go. The board isn't happy.

title: Footy Tonight want cameras in the rooms
text: Trish Lomax wants a behind-the-scenes piece while you're winning.

choices.label: Let the cameras in
choices.result: The cameras are in. Some of the players hate it.

choices.label: The rooms stay ours
choices.result: No cameras. The network isn't happy.

title: {name} wants to front the group
text: You kept {name} in when the papers wanted him out. He asks for five minutes with the group at the review to answer the papers' story himself.

choices.label: Let him front the group

effects.why: You let him front the group

effects.held_result: {name} takes the group through it and they hear him out.
effects.failed_result: It does not land with the group.

choices.rule: The group listens to a player with Leadership {holds_at} or more, or {holds_trust_at} or more if he trusts you. {name}: Leadership {leadership}.

choices.label: Keep it between you two

effects.why: You kept it between you two when he asked for the group

choices.result: You talk it through with {name} alone.

title: They say {name} is in the wrong spot
text: A former player on the radio says {name} should be playing as a {trial_word}. {first} wants to know if you will try it.

choices.label: Leave him where he is

effects.why: You said no when he asked to try the move

choices.result: {name} stays in his role.

choices.label: Try him as a {trial_word}

effects.why: You tried him in the role he asked about

choices.result: You try {name} as a {trial_word}.

unanswered.why: You said nothing when he asked about the move
unanswered.text: You say nothing. {first} is left waiting for an answer.

title: {name} passed his trial as a {trial_word}
text: {first} averaged a Player rating of {trial_avg} as a {trial_word} over the three games. Players who started as a {trial_word} this year average a Player rating of {trial_par}. {trial_tail}

choices.label: Good to hear
choices.result: {name} is back in his usual spot.

title: {name}'s trial as a {trial_word} is over
text: {first} averaged a Player rating of {trial_avg} as a {trial_word} over the three games. Players who started as a {trial_word} this year average a Player rating of {trial_par}. {trial_tail}

choices.label: Fair enough
choices.result: {name} is back in his usual spot.

title: Grand Final week
text: The Brownlow on Monday, media day, the parade on Friday. Somewhere in there, you have to train.

choices.label: Do all of it
choices.result: The players soak up every minute, and they're tired by Friday.

choices.label: The bare minimum
choices.result: In and out of the parade, no Brownlow. The sponsors grumble to the board.

title: {paper} has {club} finishing {pred_word}
text: {writer} has the club finishing {pred_word} this season, outside the finals. The papers want your answer.

unanswered.text: You say nothing. The papers have the last word.

choices.label: Say it is about right
choices.result: You tell the press the list is about where they have it.

choices.label: Say the ladder is settled on the field
choices.result: You tell the press the ladder is settled on the field, not in the papers.

choices.label: Say the club will finish {claim_word} or better
choices.result: You tell the press the club will finish {claim_word} or better.

title: {paper} asks how long you have
text: {writer} has the club finishing {pred_word}. The board's goal is to {goal_line}. He asks whether you are under pressure.

unanswered.text: You say nothing. The question stays in the papers.

choices.label: Say the board is entitled to ask
choices.result: You tell the press the board is entitled to ask, and so are they.

choices.label: Say you only think about Round 1
choices.result: You tell the press you only think about Round 1.

choices.label: Say the club will finish {claim_word} or better
choices.result: You tell the press the club will finish {claim_word} or better.

title: {writer} tips {name} to break out
text: {writer} says {name} is the one to watch this year, and asks whether you agree.

unanswered.why: You said nothing when the papers tipped him
unanswered.text: You say nothing. {first} reads it on his own.

choices.label: Say he has earned the attention

effects.why: You backed him when the papers tipped him

choices.result: You tell the press {name} has earned the attention.

choices.label: Say he still has plenty to prove

effects.why: You played down the papers' tip

choices.result: You tell the press {name} still has plenty to prove.

choices.label: Promise him a run in the side

effects.why: You promised him a run after the papers tipped him

choices.result: You tell the press {name} will get a run in the side.

title: {club} is {ladder_word}; you said {words_word}
text: Before the season you told the press {club} would finish {words_word} or better. It sits {ladder_word}, and the papers have printed your words back.

unanswered.text: You say nothing. The papers keep your words in print.

choices.label: Say you got it wrong
choices.result: You tell the press you were too bold.

choices.label: Say the season is not over
choices.result: You tell the press the season is not over.
